title: The Problem-Preservation Trap
equation: Preservation Risk = Revenue from the Problem ÷ Revenue from Solving It
hook: If your business makes more money when the problem sticks around, be honest with yourself about that.
statement: Organizations quietly keep alive the very problem they were built to solve.
explainer: When income depends on a problem existing, solving it ends the paycheck. So things drift toward managing problems forever. The more the problem pays, the harder it is to cure.
sop: Name a problem your business gets paid to handle.
Add up the Revenue from the Problem that only flows while it lasts.
Add up the Revenue from Solving It for good.
Divide to get your Preservation Risk.
Rework pricing so you earn more from fixing than managing.
equation_example: $900k a year while the problem sticks around. $100k one-time for solving it. $900k ÷ $100k = 9. Way above 1 means the problem pays more than the cure. Near or below 1 means solving it actually pays.
question: Write down one recurring fee that depends on your customer's problem never fully going away.
closing_statement: Watch who profits from the wound staying open.
caption:
Principle Nº 339: The Problem-Preservation Trap

If your business makes more money when the problem sticks around, be honest with yourself about that.

Organizations quietly keep alive the very problem they were built to solve.
